[Date submitted]

Aetna Appeals  
[Appeals mailing address from the denial notice or EOB]

Re: Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Taylor Foster  
Member ID: W492196775  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA, Wyoming  
Reference number: POC-C65CA65DA3-33163  
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy  
CPT code: 29914  
Date of denial notice: August 24, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document extensive conservative treatment, including supervised physical therapy, activity modification, NSAID treatment, and an injection, without adequate or lasting relief.

Aetna’s publicly available Hip Preservation Surgery Clinical Policy Bulletin, CPB 0736, identifies CPT 29914 as hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty for treatment of a cam lesion. The policy states that medical necessity requires:

“Failure to respond to all available conservative treatment options including: activity modification (e.g., restriction of athletic pursuits and avoidance of symptomatic motion), pharmacological intervention (e.g., non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs [NSAIDS]), injections of local anesthetics into the joint) and physiotherapy. The treatment should be for at least 12 weeks in the past year with at least 6 weeks being formal physiotherapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist not virtual). Physical therapy (PT) needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history”

The records address this requirement as follows:

1. Physical therapy and activity modification  
   The physical therapy discharge note documents 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, with activity modification, from April 27, 2026, through August 3, 2026. I completed 18 visits. This exceeds the policy’s stated 12-week treatment period and documents the required conservative-care trial. The physical therapy discharge note is included for review.

2. Medication  
   I used NSAIDs for eight months, but they provided inadequate relief.

3. Injection  
   I received a corticosteroid injection on June 14, 2026. It provided only four weeks of partial relief, after which the symptoms persisted.

4. Failure of conservative treatment  
   Despite 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, activity modification, eight months of NSAIDs, and an injection, I continue to have progressive hip pain. My symptoms have lasted 24 months and are unrelieved by rest. I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting and cannot run or squat.

The clinical records also document the condition for which CPT 29914 was requested. The July 11, 2026 MRI arthrogram shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoro-acetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. The joint space is preserved and the imaging documents Tonnis grade 0.

The policy also states:

“Diagnosis of definite femoro-acetabular impingement (FAI) defined by appropriate imaging studies (X-rays, MRI or CT scans), showing labral pathology (e.g. partial or full thickness labral tearing or labral damage) with one or more of the following: cam impingement (alpha angle greater than 50 degrees)”

The MRI arthrogram documents the labral tear and cam impingement, and the alpha angle is 68 degrees, exceeding the stated threshold.

The policy further states:

“Moderate to severe symptoms typical of FAI (hip or groin pain that is worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that significantly limits activities, with duration of at least 6 months where diagnosis of FAI has been made as above)”

My symptoms have continued for 24 months, significantly limit activity, and are worsened by sitting and pivoting. I cannot run or squat. The examination also documents positive provocative testing.

The policy additionally states:

“Absence of advanced osteoarthritis change on pre-operative X-ray (Tonnis grade 2 or more) or severe cartilage injury (Outerbridge grade III or IV)”

The imaging documents preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0, supporting the absence of advanced osteoarthritis.

For these reasons, the denial reason is not supported by the submitted clinical records. The records document more than the required duration of conservative care, formal supervised physical therapy, medication treatment, activity modification, and injection treatment, with persistent disabling symptoms and objective imaging findings.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty, CPT 29914, as requested by Okafor, MD. If Aetna believes any additional documentation is required, please identify the specific missing record or criterion and provide the complete clinical review criteria and policy version applied to this determination.

Please send the appeal decision and any request for additional information to me and to my treating surgeon. This appeal is submitted before the February 20, 2027 deadline stated in the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Taylor Foster
